newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight rates rise for 3rd straight day.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight rates rise for 3rd straight day.

text.p: Manila overnight money rose for the third straight day on Wednesday as liquidity tightened in the wake of reverse repo and T-bill purchases by banks, traders said.

Rates hit a day-high of 12.75 percent, with a low of 11.25 percent. Volume was higher at 25.372 billion pesos from 23.282 billion pesos recorded on Tuesday. Net borrowers and net lenders were equal at 32 each.

Earlier this week, banks placed 3.5 billion pesos in T-bills and 3.0 billion pesos in two-year T-notes, dealers said. Overnight rates rose as dealers anticipated that settlements starting on Wednesday would cause liquidity to tighten, dealers said.
Liquidity has also been tight because, in the past two weeks, some 6.6 billion pesos have been drained from the system after the Central Bank sold dollars to banks, they said.

A Reuters survey of eight financial institutions showed they quoted offer rates ranging from 11.30 to 11.625 for three-month bills, six-month at 11.75 to 11.825; and one-year at 11.95 to 12.25. --LILIAN KARUNUNGAN (632) 841-8937
